paper_title: Highly ordered bimolecular crystalline blends for low-noise and high-detectivity polymeric photodiodes

knowledge_points.content: The study utilizes a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) system composed of poly(2,5-bis(3-tetradecyllthiophene-2-yl)thieno[3,2-b]thiophene) (pBTTT) as the donor and phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) as the acceptor, which forms a bimolecular crystalline structure.
knowledge_points.evidence: For the model bulk heterojunction (BHJ) system, we used poly(2,5-bis(3-tetradecyllthiophene-2-yl)- thieno[3,2-b]thiophene) (pBTTT) as the donor and phenyl-C61- butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) as the acceptor... pBTTT:PCBM BHJ is known to form bimolecular crystalline structure when a eutectic composition (~44% PCBM) is used.

knowledge_points.content: The optimized polymeric photodiode with 80% PCBM content achieved a specific detectivity (D*) of 1.95 x 10^12 Jones at a -5 V bias and 430 nm illumination wavelength.
knowledge_points.evidence: The photodiode with 80% PCBM content showed the highest D* values of 1.95 x 10^12 Jones at -5 V and illumination wavelength of 430 nm.

knowledge_points.content: The pBTTT:PCBM photodiodes exhibit a high linear dynamic range (LDR) of 94 dB and a 3 dB bandwidth of 1 kHz.
knowledge_points.evidence: The resulting optimized photodiodes with 80% PCBM content showed a high detectivity value of 1.95 x 10^12 Jones, a high bandwidth of 1 kHz, and a high 94 dB linear dynamic range.

knowledge_points.content: The intercalation of PCBM between the side chains of pBTTT increases the lamellar d-spacing from 21.15 Å in pristine films to 30.2 Å in the blend films.
knowledge_points.evidence: The GIXD patterns of the pristine pBTTT films were consistent with previous reports by showing (m00) Bragg diffraction peak series up to (400) along the qz axis, with a lamellar d-spacing of 21.15 Å... all the other GIXD patterns obtained from the pBTTT:PCBM BHJ films with various blend ratios showed increased lamellar d-spacing of 30.2 Å.

knowledge_points.content: The paracrystalline disorder parameter (g) for pBTTT:PCBM blend films remains low (approximately 3-4%), indicating high crystalline perfection similar to pristine pBTTT (g = 3.4%).
knowledge_points.evidence: Interestingly, all the blend films revealed a low level of paracrystalline disorder (g = ~3–4%), which is even similar to that of the pristine pBTTT film (g = 3.4%).

knowledge_points.content: Structural perfection in the bimolecular crystalline active layer reduces energetic disorder, which suppresses undesired charge injection into localized energy states during reverse saturation operation, leading to low dark currents (< 4 nA/cm² at -5 V).
knowledge_points.evidence: Structural localization (caused by either lattice disorder or orientation disorder) gives rise to energetic disorder... the obtained relatively low paracrystalline disorder (g = ~3–4%) and high degree of orientation ordering of pBTTT:PCBM can lead to low dark current... all the other blend films yielded a significant low-dark-current behavior with a current density less than 4 nA cm^-2 at -5 V.

knowledge_points.content: Active layers were fabricated by spin-coating pBTTT:PCBM from chlorobenzene at a concentration of 40 mg/mL, followed by thermal annealing at 190 °C for 5 minutes to enhance intermolecular crystalline order.
knowledge_points.evidence: All the BHJ films with varying weight ratio of the blend were annealed at 190 °C for 5 min to increase the intermolecular crystalline order... solubilized overnight in chlorobenzene (CB) at a total concentration of 40 mg mL^-1.

knowledge_points.content: The 1 kHz bandwidth of the pBTTT:PCBM photodiodes is transit-time limited, as evidenced by the increase in bandwidth with higher reverse bias and the close agreement between measured and theoretical bandwidth (1.393 kHz).
knowledge_points.evidence: As the reverse bias was increased to negative values, the 3 dB bandwidth tended to increase, implying that the bandwidth was transit-time limited... The calculated theoretical estimation of the bandwidth is 1.393 kHz, which is very close to the actually measured bandwidth value of 1 kHz.

knowledge_points.content: Pole figure analysis of pBTTT:PCBM blends indicates a preferential edge-on crystalline orientation, with edge-on to face-on area ratios (Aedge-on/Aface-on) ranging from 0.8 to 0.9.
knowledge_points.evidence: the values of Aedge-on/Aface-on obtained from all the other blend films also ranged from 0.8 to 0.9, indicating that preferential edge-on structures were retained even for an excess amount of PCBM.
